payload.set_intro: A $25.0\text{ mL}$ sample of a weak monoprotic acid, HA, is titrated with $0.100\text{ M}$ NaOH. The titration curve is shown.

stimulus.description: Titration of 25.0 mL of 0.100 M weak acid HA with 0.100 M NaOH

items.stem: Which of the following is the best estimate of the acid dissociation constant, $K_a$, of HA?

options.why: Uses the pH at the equivalence point instead of the pH at the half-equivalence point.
The equivalence point is at 25.0 mL (the steep rise), so the half-equivalence point is at 12.5 mL, where pH = pKa. The curve shows pH ≈ 4.30 there, so Ka = 10^−4.30 = 5.00 × 10⁻⁵.
Uses the initial pH of the acid solution instead of the pH at the half-equivalence point.
Uses the pH after excess base was added instead of the pH at the half-equivalence point.
